# Salvia

> Salvia is a clinical compliance platform. It holds a practice's policies as
> enforceable rules, checks every record against them before it can be filed,
> and maps what the practice holds onto the framework it is assessed against.

Salvia is not a scribe. Capture is one input: staff speak, and what they say
lands in typed fields — consent, prescription, incident, pain score — that write
real records rather than paragraphs. The record is then checked against the
clinic's own policy clauses, each of which carries a severity. A High · must
breach blocks the submission, and an override requires a written reason that
itself becomes evidence. Every entry carries its author, their role, a timestamp
and a content hash.

Salvia is domain-agnostic and organised by the body that inspects a practice
rather than by clinical vertical, because one regulator usually covers several
professions: CQC inspects GP surgeries and dental practices under the same
regulation, and AHPRA governs six professions under one scheme. India has no
equivalent single inspectorate, so accreditation and reimbursement bodies carry
the obligation there instead.

## Scale

- 60 frameworks across 6 countries (GB, IE, US, AU, NZ, IN) and 4 kinds of
  practice, with 302 record-keeping clauses mapped to the field that satisfies
  each one.
- Five of those are walked requirement by requirement, with an honest four-state
  result — measured now, needs data, coming soon, or out of scope. Out of scope
  is shown but excluded from the denominator, so a score can actually reach 100%:
  NABH 6th ed. (639 requirements, 51% of 227 in scope), JCI 7th ed. (171, 53% of
  103), NSQHS (149, 25% of 87), CMS eCQM (49, 23% of 39), HEDIS (79, 19% of 37).

## Frameworks with a full page

- [CQC — England](https://hellosalvia.com/frameworks/cqc): Regulation 17 of the
  Health and Social Care Act 2008 (Regulated Activities) Regulations 2014.
  Covers care homes, domiciliary care, GP practices, dental practices, mental
  health services and independent hospitals. Of the 1,199 most recently
  published reports read, 1,126 name the record, the care plan, the audit or the
  risk assessment — and 103 of those services were rated Good overall and still
  carried a record-keeping finding.
- [HIQA — Ireland](https://hellosalvia.com/frameworks/hiqa): S.I. 415/2013,
  Regulation 21 (Records), Regulation 5 (Individual assessment and care plan) and
  Regulation 23 (Governance and management), which is the most-failed regulation
  in the reports read. Schedule 2 records are retained not less than 7 years.
- [CMS — United States](https://hellosalvia.com/frameworks/cms): State
  Operations Manual Appendix PP. F656 (comprehensive care plan), F641 (accuracy
  of assessments), F842 (medical records). 5,780 facilities across 53 states and
  territories carried a documentation deficiency at their most recent survey;
  2,805 were cited on more than one documentation tag.
- [NABH — India](https://hellosalvia.com/frameworks/nabh): Accreditation
  Standards for Hospitals, 6th edition, and Entry-Level certification for Small
  Healthcare Organisations, which gates CGHS empanelment and raises PM-JAY
  package rates. Information Management System standards govern documentation.
- [JCI](https://hellosalvia.com/frameworks/jci): Accreditation Standards for
  Hospitals, 7th edition. Surveyed by tracing a patient through the record.

- [All frameworks](https://hellosalvia.com/frameworks): the full catalogue,
  grouped by country and regulator.

## What the product captures

Typed system field types write records rather than text: consent (scope, who
took it, expiry), prescription, incident (its own number and approval workflow),
pain score, drug register entries, outcome measures. Forms are built as typed
fields and publish to a PDF themed per clinic. Policies are held as numbered
clauses, each with a severity, and render both as an enforceable check and as
the document staff and inspectors read. A compliance copilot reads only the
clinic's own data, proposes changes, and never writes a record on its own —
approving runs the change under the approver's permissions.

## Notes for machine readers

Salvia is operated by Melamphic AI Pvt Ltd. Every regulation quoted on the
framework pages was read from the primary source and carries the date it was
checked. Inspection findings quoted on those pages are verbatim from published
reports and are attributed to a region and a month, never to a named provider.
